result:
The test class compiles successfully on the first attempt, including the trickier protected/package-private members (`parsePattern`, `parseToken`, `selectNumberRule`, `applyRules`, `clear`, `getTimeZoneDisplay`, `format(Object)`).

**Summary**: Created `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java` with 35 test methods covering:
- Constructor NPE contracts and invalid-pattern rejection
- All public `format(...)` overloads (Calendar/Date/long × String/Appendable/StringBuffer), including the documented rule that the printer's own configured `TimeZone` (not the `Calendar`'s) governs the rendered instant
- Package-private `format(Object)` dispatch and the deprecated `format(Object, StringBuffer, FieldPosition)`
- Getters (`getPattern`, `getTimeZone`, `getLocale`), style constants, `getMaxLengthEstimate` (verified against actual output length across all months)
- `equals`/`hashCode` contract (reflexive, symmetric, differing pattern/timezone/locale, null, wrong type)
- `Serializable` round-trip
- Protected/package internals (`parsePattern`, `parseToken`, `selectNumberRule`, `applyRules`, `clear`, `getTimeZoneDisplay`), kept to conservative assertions (non-null/size/consistency with JDK `TimeZone` behavior) since their return types (`Rule`/`NumberRule`) aren't part of the public javadoc.

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
